In this paper, we provide a theoretical analysis of the conditions under which the performance of the Gaussian Smoothing Zeroth-Order Optimization (ZSG) algorithm exceeds that of the coordinate sketching version of the SEGA algorithm. Our key finding is that ZSG exhibits weak dimensional dependence and can outperform ZSC when the eigenvalues of the Hessian matrix are significantly different.
